 Judgment
1.

This appeal is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the I Addl. Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Kalaburagi, (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.1198/2012 dated 16.01.2015.

2. Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. The brief facts of the case are:
That the deceased Sharnappa was aged about 37 years, hale and healthy and he was working as Coolie and Agriculturist and earning Rs.12,000/- per month and he was contributing the said income to the welfare of his family.
On 4.4.2012 at about 7.00 pm.

the deceased Sharnappa and others were sitting on the Katta of the bridge at Savelshoware cross on Aland-Waggada road, at that time one Lorry beating Reg.No.MH-12/FZ-4280 came from Aland check post which was driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner and in high speed and dashed to the deceased and other persons due to which the deceased Sharnappa sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Therefore, the claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation of Rs.13,50,000/-.
5. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim made by the claimants and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
7. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P6.
On the other hand, respondent No.2-Insurer did not adduce evidence.
8. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
9. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal considered awarded the compensation at Rs.6,52,500/-.

10. Insofar as liability to pay the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal noticed the documents placed on record and respondent No.2 being the insurer, fastened the liability on it to pay the compensation.
11. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and award, the claimants have filed the present appeal.
12. The learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Tribunal committed an error in considering the income of the deceased.
He contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced.

He further contended that the Tribunal ought to have been awarded compensation towards loss of consortium at the rate of Rs.40,000/- to each of the Smt.Gourabai W/O Sharanappa vs Sri.Abhinay R.Lunkad S/O Ramanlal ...

13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The insurer of the offending vehicle on the other hand contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was also negligent in the accident and therefore, the Tribunal ought to have proportionately fixed the liability on the owner of the vehicle.
14. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
15. In the absence of any evidence or proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2012, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.6,500/- p.m. as per chart.

In view of the law laid down by the Constitutional Bench of the Supreme Court in NATIONAL INSURANCE CO., LTD., VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, to the aforesaid amount, 40% has to be added on account of future prospects as the deceased was aged about 37 years.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE CO., LTD., VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the monthly income considered as Rs.9,100/-.

Out of which, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th towards personal expenses and therefore, the monthly income comes to Rs.6,825/-
(Rs.9,100/- - Rs.2,275/-).

16. As on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged 37 years, as per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of SARLA VERMA (SMT) & OTHERS VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION & ANOTHER, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier applied to the age group of the claimant is 15, which is rightly taken by the tribunal.

entities.text: SARLA VERMA (SMT) & OTHERS VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION & ANOTHER, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.12,28,500/- (Rs.6,825/- x 12 x 15) on account of loss of dependency as against Rs.6,07,500/- awarded by the Tribunal.

17. In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM & OTHERS reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, each of the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of consortium'.

entities.text: MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM & OTHERS reported in 2018 ACJ 2782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,60,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 4) as against Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

18. The claimants are also entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- under conventional heads as against Rs.20,000/- and Rs.15,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards love and affection and funeral and transportation charges.
19. Thus, the claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.14,18,500/- as against Rs.6,52,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, the claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.7,66,500/-.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER Smt.Gourabai W/O Sharanappa vs Sri.Abhinay R.Lunkad S/O Ramanlal ...

(a) The appeal is allowed in part.

(b) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.14,18,500/- as against Rs.6,52,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
(c) The claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.7,66,500/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till the date of realization of amount.

(d) The Respondent No.2, Insurance  Company is directed to deposit the  enhanced compensation amount along with interest, within a period of eight - 10 - weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
(e) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the jurisdictional Tribunal for disbursement.
(f) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
